name: review_status
description: Check the current Monocle review status. Returns whether feedback is pending, a pause was requested, or no feedback is available.

name: get_feedback
description: Retrieve review feedback from Monocle. With wait=true, blocks until the reviewer submits feedback. The review's heading states the verdict: 'Approved' means done; 'Changes Requested' means address the comments and resubmit; 'Questions' means the reviewer wants answers rather than edits — answer them and continue, changing code only where an answer turns out to require it, then submit again. Questions block you in the same way changes do, since the reviewer is waiting, but do not rewrite code merely to have something to show.

name: send_artifact
description: Send content to Monocle for the reviewer to see. Provide content directly or pass file_path to read from disk. Media files (images, video, audio — .png/.jpg/.gif/.webp/.svg/.mp4/.mov/.webm/.mp3/.wav, etc.) passed via file_path are sent as media artifacts: Monocle copies the file into managed storage and the reviewer opens it in a media viewer (default Google Chrome). Use this to submit screenshots, diagrams, or recordings for review.

name: add_files
description: Add EXTRA context files to the review as full-content views — files you want the reviewer to see that are NOT part of the change (e.g. an unchanged interface, schema, or config the change depends on). Do NOT use this to define the set of files under review: uncommitted changes are shown automatically, and committed work is shown by calling set_base_ref (which renders every changed file as a diff). Files already in the review — whether uncommitted or in a base-ref range — are skipped here rather than duplicated as full-content views, so passing your changed files is a no-op. In short: set_base_ref for the diff, add_files only for surrounding context outside it.

name: remove_files
description: Remove previously-added context files (added via add_files) from the current Monocle review session. Pass the same paths used with add_files. This only affects extra context files; it does not remove base-ref diffs (change the range with set_base_ref instead).

name: set_file_groups
description: Organize the changed files in Monocle's grouped sidebar view for the reviewer. Provide entries, each with a path (matching a changed file from review_status) and optional grouping metadata: workstream (optional top-level grouping above the group — use it when the change spans multiple independent efforts/features, e.g. two parallel workstreams, so files nest as workstream → group → files; omit it for a single-workstream change), workstream_order (integer; lower workstreams shown first), group (free-form label like "UI", "Backend", "Database" to tell the change as a top-down story), group_order (integer; lower groups shown first), sort_index (order within a group; lower first), category (one of code/test/config/docs/build to override the path heuristic), and criticality (integer; higher = more important). Order workstreams and groups from entry-point to dependency (e.g. UI → API → database) so the reviewer reads the change in flow order. Set replace=true to replace all prior grouping. The reviewer presses 'f' to cycle to the grouped view.

name: add_annotations
description: Attach short rationale notes to specific ranges of the changed code to guide the reviewer, each linking out to the docs that motivate it. These annotations are shown to the reviewer only — they are NOT review feedback and are never sent back to you. Provide entries: file (a changed-file path from review_status), line_start and line_end (the exact code range the note explains), summary (one line: why this code exists / what it does), and refs — an array of doc links, each with kind ('file' for a repo path or 'artifact' for a sent artifact id), doc (the path or artifact id), label (link text), and a line/column range into that doc (start_line, start_col, end_line, end_col; 1-based lines, 0-based cols) pointing at the relevant passage in a TODO or design doc. Keep summaries to one line; attach multiple refs when several docs apply. Set replace=true to clear all prior annotations first (default replaces per file). The reviewer clicks or keys through the refs to open the doc passage beside the code. The response reports how many were accepted and lists any rejected entries with reasons (e.g. line_end < line_start, or a file that isn't in the review) plus warnings for doc refs that don't resolve — read it and resend corrected entries. Annotations are cleared automatically when the reviewer submits and the round advances, so re-annotate against the new code each round. The reviewer can reply to an annotation with an `answer` comment, which asks nothing further of you.

name: set_review_name
description: Start/name a review. The name (a brief title, e.g. 'Add OAuth login') is shown in Monocle's top bar AND marks the review as in-progress; this is how you begin a review. Rules: the name is required and must be non-empty (only the reviewer closes a review, by approving or clearing). Calling it again with the SAME name is a no-op. Calling it with a NEW name while a review is already open silently replaces the old one IF the reviewer hasn't left any comments; if the reviewer HAS commented, it is refused — pass force=true to discard their in-progress review and start yours. So: call this once at the start of each review; don't rename mid-review.

name: set_base_ref
description: Review changes you have already committed. Set the commit to diff against (ref) — e.g. the branch you started from, a SHA, or HEAD~N — and Monocle shows everything since it, including your commits, for review. The ref's own changes are excluded. By default Monocle only shows uncommitted working-tree changes, so call this when your work is committed. The base reverts to HEAD automatically once the reviewer submits. Pass reset=true to go back to working-tree review immediately.

name: send_diff
description: Show the reviewer a before/after comparison whose contents you supply directly — for illustrating a change rather than reviewing one. Use it for pseudocode before/after, two competing design options side by side, or any contrast that is NOT the state of the repository. Pass name (a title for the comparison) and pairs: an array of { label, before, after, lang }, where before/after are the two texts, label names that pane (it need not be a real file), and lang is an optional syntax-highlighting hint like "go" or "py". An empty or omitted before renders as an all-new file. Send several pairs to give the reviewer multiple switchable diffs — e.g. one pair per design option sharing the same before. Nothing on disk is read and no git command runs, so this is safe with a dirty working tree and does not disturb a review already in progress. Re-sending the same name/label updates that comparison in place. This is NOT how you get your actual code changes reviewed — committed work uses set_base_ref and uncommitted work is shown automatically.

name: set_repo
description: Point Monocle at the repository/worktree you are actually working in. Pass path — any path inside that repo (usually its root or your current working directory); Monocle finds the enclosing repo root and routes every subsequent review tool (review_status, send_artifact, set_base_ref, add_files, get_feedback, …) to that repo's engine. Empty path means the current working directory. CALL THIS ONCE, before the first review action, whenever your working directory is not where the MCP server was launched — most importantly right after entering a git worktree (e.g. a per-lane worktree in a multi-agent setup). Without it, agents launched from a shared directory all bind to the same engine and silently overwrite one another's review; a running engine is started for the repo automatically if none exists. The response names the repo it bound to — confirm it matches your worktree.
